items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played a composition called “Brother K” that he had written for Martin Luther King

ctx.x: Yep, he was my friend right up to till the day he died. From that party, he went in and out of the hospital in December. He died finally on the 6th of January, 1993. I was in Oberlin at the time and I called the attorney who was putting together the memorial service. I told him that I wanted to perform. He says, “Oh, we have you down to perform with the trumpets.” I said, “I don’t want to perform with the trumpets. I want to perform by myself. Solo, and I want to talk about Dizzy Gillespie,” which I did do.

And the video is very nice; they taped his whole funeral. I played a composition called “Brother K” that he had written for Martin Luther King, and I ended that with “Nobody Knows The Trouble I’ve Seen.” I’ve played that song many, many times at musician’s funerals, and dedications for musicians because I really feel it says something very, very poignant about the jazz artist. He or she can get there perform in a happy fashion, and you really don’t know what they have gone through in the past hours, days or…
